A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same OmniZip study and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–F. Material moved between the main text and appendix can be matched reliably.

before.justification: Section 4 and Appendix E report original benchmark evaluations, inference-efficiency measurements, and ablations using Qwen2.5-Omni-7B and 3B.

after.justification: Section 4 and Appendix E retain original benchmark, efficiency, and ablation results, including the G sensitivity study relocated to the appendix.

M1.justification: Audio-token selection, cross-modal anchor consolidation, audio-guided video pruning, and interleaved spatio-temporal compression remain unchanged. Sections 3.3–3.4 and Appendix A describe the same procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate AVUT, VideoMME, ShortVid-Bench, and WorldSense with the same task and domain coverage. Newly cited OmniVideoBench and LVOmniBench are not added to the evaluations.

E2.justification: The corresponding comparisons retain the same baselines: full tokens, Random, FastV, and DyCoke (V&A), with VisionZip retained in Table 4's token-selection ablation. Added references do not introduce evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: The model scales, retention settings, FLOPs-based comparison protocol, frame limits, and evaluation procedures are unchanged. Appendix C retains the same computational-cost accounting with R = 100 generated tokens.

E4.justification: The attention analysis, pruning-ratio sensitivity, component ablations, token-selection comparisons, and supplementary pruning comparisons are retained. The G study moves from Section 4.4/Figure 7 to Appendix E/Figure 8 without changing its analysis or results.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The revision introduces no statistical estimation or uncertainty-reporting changes.

E6.justification: Table 2 changes OmniZip-7B at 45% retention from 50.1 to 49.4 for Tech & Science and from 47.6 to 45.6 for Daily Life. Its 45.9 average and corresponding Table 6 values remain unchanged. The introduction also changes the upper speedup figure from 3.54× to 3.42×; other matched numerical results are retained.

T1.justification: Equations 1–9, Algorithm 1, and the computational derivation remain unchanged. Correcting Nd to Nv in the token-count description and fixing the spelling of Euclidean are notation and language corrections, not mathematical revisions.

C1.justification: The introduction narrows its stated speedup range from 2.51–3.54× to 2.51–3.42×, aligning it with the existing measurements. The central novelty, training-free operation, joint audio-video compression, and accuracy-efficiency claims otherwise remain unchanged.

C2.justification: The audio-locality interpretation, task-dependent compression tradeoffs, applicability discussion, and offline-inference limitation are retained. The FlashAttention/OOM discussion added to Section 2.2 already appeared in v1 Appendix D.3, and the G interpretation is simply relocated.

D1.justification: The code link, hardware specifications, frame caps, token counts, pruning hyperparameters, and implementation descriptions are unchanged. No new reproducibility information or resource-access instructions are supplied.

R1.justification: The bibliography adds nine works, including LLaVA-OneVision-1.5, OmniVideoBench, LVOmniBench, Video Compression Commander, and OBS-Diff. These extend the citations without substantially changing the paper's research positioning or novelty argument.

P1.justification: The abstract and scattered passages receive copyediting, author-name and terminology corrections, and expanded acknowledgements. Existing appendix discussion is repeated in Section 2.2, and the G ablation text moves to Appendix E; the overall narrative remains intact.

P2.justification: Figure 2's zoomed heatmaps gain triangular masking, Figure 3's compression label is corrected, and table spacing and captions are adjusted. Table 3 is repositioned, while the G plot moves to the appendix and Figures 7–8 exchange numbering.

improvement.justification: Copyediting and the 3.54× to 3.42× speedup correction improve clarity, but v2 introduces conflicting benchmark reporting: Table 2's revised 49.4/45.6 scores disagree with Table 6's retained 50.1/47.6, which matched in v1. Table 2 also still bolds 45.6 as best despite higher scores in that column. This unexplained inconsistency weakens empirical reporting reliability more than the limited editorial improvements strengthen it.
